The test image shows a tomato stem with white/light-colored powdery or crusty deposits scattered along the stem surface. The trichomes (stem hairs) are visible. Leaves in background appear green/healthy. Key candidates: Powdery Mildew (white coating on stems), Bacterial Speck (small raised spots), Bacterial Canker (stem lesions).

Now viewing one reference from each of 4 candidate classes:

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Tomato stem with scattered white/crusty granular deposits along the stem surface. Trichomes visible. Background leaves appear green/healthy.
- **Powdery Mildew ref**: White powdery patches on leaves — matches the white powdery texture seen in the test stem deposits.
- **Bacterial Speck ref**: Dark/black small spots on leaves — does not match white stem deposits.
- **Bacterial Canker ref**: Stem rot, yellowing, wilting — does not match.
- **Alternaria ref**: Dark brown cankers on stems — does not match white deposits.

The white powdery/granular deposits on the tomato stem most closely match **Powdery Mildew**, which causes white fungal growth on stems as well as leaves. No dark lesions, no wilting, no necrotic cankers — just surface white deposits consistent with powdery mildew sporulation.
